That gap concerns lifting internally disjoint paths through an edge contraction. Here contracting each forced tile triangle is used only to test connectivity: all and only selected cross edges join different triangles, so no path-lifting inference is made.

results.claim: The arbitrary-sharing-number no-teleport problem belongs to NP.
results.proof_sketch: Let L be the total number of feature occurrences. Every legal no-teleport transition has distinct endpoint tiles with a common live feature and therefore deletes at least those two occurrences. Thus every play has at most floor(L/2) transitions. A certificate is a starting tile followed by that polynomial-length tile sequence. A verifier tracks live occurrences, checks distinct consecutive tiles and a nonempty live intersection, deletes every feature live at both endpoints, and finally checks that no occurrence remains, all in polynomial time. Also, an unordered tile pair cannot recur: its first use deletes every then-live common feature, and deleted occurrences never become live again.

results.claim: There is an exact characterization by perfect matchings plus an ordered Euler trail with precedence constraints.
results.proof_sketch: For each feature f with support S_f, choose a perfect matching M_f, and let H be the simple set union of the M_f. A shared matching edge appears once in H because one transition simultaneously deletes every live feature common to its endpoints. Write m_f(v) for v's matching edge. The characterization requires an Euler-trail order tau of H such that for every e=uv in H\M_f with u,v in S_f, either m_f(u) precedes e or m_f(v) precedes e. Necessity follows from any play: f-deletions pair S_f, every move deletes some feature, no tile pair recurs, and a nonmatching f-edge can occur only after f has disappeared at an endpoint. For sufficiency, suppose the earliest matching event m_f(u) that should delete f fails because u lost f on an earlier nonmatching edge uw. Since m_f(u) is later, precedence forces m_f(w) before uw. By earliestness, m_f(w) successfully deleted f at w, so uw could not have deleted f at u, a contradiction. Hence all matching events succeed. Every H-edge belongs to some matching, so every transition is legal, and all occurrences are deleted. The featureless case uses the empty trail.

results.claim: If every occurring feature appears on exactly two tiles, no-teleport solvability is decidable in linear time even with unbounded sharing number.
results.proof_sketch: Build a simple graph K on edge-bearing tiles, with edge uv when at least one feature has support {u,v}. Such a feature can be deleted only by transition uv, and all features with the same endpoint pair remain synchronized and are deleted together; hence their shared edge has multiplicity one in K. A solution is therefore exactly an Euler trail using every edge of K. The featureless instance is trivially solved; otherwise the criterion is connectivity of the edge-bearing vertices and zero or two odd degrees. In the standard word-RAM model with array-indexed feature and tile identifiers, scan the L occurrences to obtain endpoint pairs, radix-sort the word-sized integer pairs, deduplicate them, and test connectivity and degree parity, all in deterministic O(L) time. The number of features sharing one pair is unrestricted.

results.claim: The obvious static relaxation—choosing feature-perfect-matchings whose simple union is Eulerian—is not sufficient.
results.proof_sketch: Take tiles 0,1,2,3,4 and feature supports {0,1}, {0,2}, {1,2}, {0,1,2,3}, and {0,1,2,4}. The first three force the core triangle. Tiles 3 and 4 each contain only their respective four-support feature, so they are the endpoints of any no-teleport play. If their incident edges attach to core vertices i and j, Euler parity forces i=j. Starting at 3, the play takes 3i, traverses the triangle as a circuit based at i, and ends with i4. Before the first triangle edge from i, the feature on {0,1,2,4} is live at every core tile; that edge deletes its occurrence at i, so the final i4 move is illegal. Reversing exchanges the two four-support features and gives the same contradiction. Yet choose matchings 03+12 and 04+12 for those features, with forced matchings 01, 02, and 12. Their simple union is {01,02,12,03,04}, connected with exactly odd vertices 3 and 4. The shared edge 12 is intentionally counted once. Thus an Eulerian simple union alone is insufficient.

results.claim: An exact state-space algorithm runs in O(n^2 L·2^L) time and O(n·2^L) space.
results.proof_sketch: Represent the live feature occurrences by an L-bit mask and memoize (current tile, live mask), giving at most n times 2^L states. From each state inspect the n-1 other tiles. A direct scan of the incidence data in O(L) time finds all features live at both endpoints; the transition is allowed exactly when this set is nonempty, and its two endpoint occurrences for every such feature are cleared. Each transition strictly lowers the live-occurrence count, so the recurrence is acyclic and exact. Trying every starting tile shares the memo table. Thus the time is O(n^2 L times 2^L), and a directly indexed memo table uses O(n times 2^L) space, apart from lower-order input and recursion storage.

results.claim: For every simple cubic graph G, one can construct in linear time a sharing-number-4 Tiles instance I(G) that is solvable without teleport moves if and only if G has a Hamiltonian cycle.
results.proof_sketch:
Let G=(V,E) be simple and 3-regular. For each x create tiles x^0,x^1,r_x and private features with supports {x^0,x^1}, {x^1,r_x}, and {r_x,x^0}, forcing a local triangle. For each edge e=xy create f_e with support {x^0,x^1,y^0,y^1}. If C is a Hamiltonian cycle, pair f_e layerwise as x^0y^0,x^1y^1 for e in C and pair it locally as x^0x^1,y^0y^1 otherwise. A legal play is explicit: traverse C on layer 0; use two sides of the starting local triangle to reach layer 1; traverse C on layer 1, splicing the complete local triangle at every nonstarting vertex; then use the starting rung last. Layer-0 deletions prevent local rungs from prematurely deleting selected features, while each unselected feature is deleted at its two endpoint rungs.

Conversely, any solution pairs the four occurrences of every f_e. Its matching is either local-local, called unselected, or one of the two cross-cross matchings, called selected. Let s_x be the number of selected input edges incident with x. In the simple move graph H, the forced triangle gives degree 2 at x^0 and x^1; every selected edge adds one distinct cross edge at each, while every unselected matching edge coincides with the forced rung. Hence deg_H(x^0)=deg_H(x^1)=2+s_x and deg_H(r_x)=2. If k input vertices have odd s_x, H has 2k odd vertices. An Euler trail has at most two, whereas the handshaking lemma makes k even, so k=0. Connectivity of H implies connectivity of the selected subgraph after contracting local triangles. Thus every s_x is positive and even; cubicity forces s_x=2. The selected edges therefore form a connected spanning 2-regular graph, namely a Hamiltonian cycle.

results.claim: Deciding no-teleport solvability is NP-hard even when the sharing number is at most 4, every feature occurs on two or four tiles, and every tile contains at most five features.
results.proof_sketch: Reduce from the standard NP-complete Hamiltonian Cycle problem on simple cubic graphs using I(G) from the preceding equivalence. The construction has 3|V| tiles and 3|V|+|E| features and is linear. A pair x^0,x^1 shares its private rung feature and the three incident edge features, so the sharing number is 4. Private features have frequency 2, edge features have frequency 4, relay tiles contain two features, and layer tiles contain five.

results.claim: The arbitrary-sharing-number no-teleport problem is NP-complete, and remains NP-complete under the restrictions in the preceding claim.
results.proof_sketch: NP-hardness follows from the cubic-Hamiltonian-cycle reduction. Membership in NP is the first preserved claim: every legal move deletes at least two of the L initial occurrences, so a solution has polynomial length and can be verified by exact simulation. The same verifier establishes membership for the restricted instances.

final_writeup:
Resolution: FULL. No-teleport Tiles solvability is NP-complete. In fact, NP-hardness already holds when the sharing number is at most 4, every feature occurs on two or four tiles, and every tile contains at most five features. This supplies the matching hardness result missing from the audited parent.

Membership in NP is unchanged. If L is the number of feature occurrences, every legal transition deletes at least two occurrences, so any solution has at most floor(L/2) transitions. A tile sequence is therefore a polynomial certificate, and the deletion rule can be simulated exactly in polynomial time.

For hardness, reduce from Hamiltonian Cycle on simple cubic graphs. Given G=(V,E), replace every vertex x by three tiles x^0,x^1,r_x. Add three private frequency-two features supported respectively on {x^0,x^1}, {x^1,r_x}, and {r_x,x^0}. Any completed play must therefore traverse all three edges of this local triangle. For every input edge e=xy, add a feature f_e supported on {x^0,x^1,y^0,y^1}.

First suppose G has a Hamiltonian cycle C=(v_0,...,v_{q-1},v_0). For every e=xy in C, use the layerwise deletion pairs x^0y^0 and x^1y^1. For every e outside C, use the local pairs x^0x^1 and y^0y^1; these coincide with already-forced local rungs.

There is a direct legal order. Traverse the whole copy of C on layer 0, returning to v_0^0. Move through r_{v_0} to v_0^1. Now traverse C on layer 1. Upon first reaching each v_i^1 with i>0, splice in the circuit v_i^1,r_{v_i},v_i^0,v_i^1 before continuing. After the layer-1 cycle returns to v_0^1, finish with the rung v_0^1v_0^0. Every move has a live private or edge feature. Traversing layer 0 has already removed the x^0 occurrence of each selected incident feature before a local rung is used, so that rung cannot delete the corresponding x^1 occurrence prematurely. Each selected f_e is deleted on its two layer edges, every unselected f_e is deleted at its two endpoint rungs, and every private feature is deleted. Thus I(G) is solvable without teleporting.

Conversely, consider any no-teleport solution. The transitions deleting a feature pair its support. For an edge feature f_e, its perfect matching is either the local-local matching x^0x^1,y^0y^1 or one of the two matchings consisting entirely of cross edges between the x- and y-triples. Call e unselected in the first case and selected otherwise, and let s_x be the number of selected input edges incident with x.

Let H be the simple graph of transitions in the solution. An unordered tile pair cannot recur, so the move sequence is an Euler trail of H. Each local triangle is present. Because G is simple, the cross edges contributed by distinct selected input edges cannot coincide. Consequently

deg_H(x^0)=deg_H(x^1)=2+s_x, while deg_H(r_x)=2.

If k vertices x have odd s_x, H has exactly 2k odd vertices. An Euler trail permits at most two odd vertices. The handshaking lemma applied to the selected subgraph says k is even, so k=0. Hence every s_x is even. Moreover, H is connected, and the only edges between different local triangles come from selected input edges. Contracting the local triangles therefore shows that the selected spanning subgraph of G is connected. Since G is cubic, every positive even s_x equals 2. The selected subgraph is consequently connected, spanning, and 2-regular, so it is a Hamiltonian cycle. This proves the equivalence and the reduction's soundness for every possible solution, not merely for the displayed construction.

The construction is linear: it has 3|V| tiles, 3|V|+|E| features, and 6|V|+4|E| occurrences. Each edge feature has frequency four and each private feature frequency two. A layer tile contains its two private features and the three incident edge features. The only pair sharing four features is x^0,x^1: its rung feature plus the three incident edge features. All other pairs share at most one. Thus the promised restrictions hold.

The five audited parent claims remain valid. In particular, solutions also admit the exact perfect-matching/Euler-order characterization with precedence constraints; the five-tile example still shows that an Eulerian simple union without the temporal constraints is insufficient. When every feature has frequency two, deduplicating its forced endpoint pair reduces the problem to an ordinary Euler-trail test in linear time, even with unbounded sharing number. The exact O(n^2 L·2^L)-time, O(n·2^L)-space state search remains available. The new reduction closes the general complexity question: the arbitrary-sharing-number problem, and already the stated sharing-number-4 subclass, is NP-complete.
